Revised assessment: The statement’s “solid” growth and low unemployment alongside “somewhat elevated” inflation, a hold at 4.25–4.50%, and continued balance-sheet runoff signal a restrictive but patient stance. This is consistent with forward‑looking New‑Keynesian guidance (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and the Fed’s documented interest‑rate smoothing behavior, as well as simple Taylor‑rule prescriptions that discourage premature easing while inflation remains above the 2% PCE target. The operational settings (IORB, standing repo/reverse repo) reflect the post‑2008 floor‑system framework and liquidity backstop principles while keeping the stance tight, aligning with Bagehot‑style discipline without easing financial conditions. Research on inflation‑at‑risk and on elevated markups/profits suggests upside inflation tail risks, justifying the Committee’s “balanced risks” and data‑dependent forward guidance. Net tone: modestly positive on growth but cautious on inflation, i.e., neutral‑to‑slightly positive overall.
